Nevertheless, I would expect a human to hesitate before making a change that automatically ends his employment that afternoon, with nobody available to review it beforehand. He faced an unexpected family emergency and notified his team leader before his shift—conduct quite different from his earlier oversleeping, and relevant to the stated purpose of probation.

Leaving SC would be a deliberate coding exception, not an accurate sickness classification. But it would keep the day unpaid without triggering dismissal, while a truthful note and email would make the discrepancy visible for subsequent review. I think that practical, compassionate workaround is more likely than mechanically changing Ryan to UA, though a particularly rule-bound employee could do the latter.
